title: Prince de Conti's ciphered mémoires to Laigue and Noirmoutier, Paris, 5, 26 and 27 March 1649, BnF fr. 3854 nos. 41-43

plaintext.source: Lasry, 'Armand de Bourbon's Poly-Homophonic Cipher - 1649', HistoCrypt 2023, §4 (full text and key)

transcription.notes: transcription.txt mixes cipher letters with bracketed clear words, so no cipher-only count was measured (2,328 letters including clear words).

plaintext.source: Contemporary interlinear decipherment from f. 117r l. 12 onward; the first 12 lines (264 groups) were never glossed

transcription.source: Gallica images, canvases 245-251; glossed groups in n43/pairs_c245-251.txt
transcription.notes: Count is the unglossed opening only; the glossed body adds about 3,300 groups (READING43.md), not measured.

system.summary: Nos. 41-42: poly-homophonic lower-case letter cipher without nomenclator; no. 43: numeric letter-and-syllable code with four interleaved alphabets, five-syllable blocks and nulls 99-250.

diacritics.note: In no. 43 an underlined number reverses its syllable (385 ra, 385 underlined ar).

system.notes: Two different systems: nos. 41-42 polyphonic a=T/P/A/B, e=E/G, i=C/Z, m=S/D/X, n=M/Q (Lasry); no. 43 uses digits, alphabetical blocks, code words 457 cardinal, 458 parlement, 472 l'archiduc. symbol_kind and summary cover both.

prior_solution.where: Nos. 41-42: Lasry, HistoCrypt 2023; no. 43 body: contemporary interlinear decipherment on the leaves (opening never deciphered)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: decode.py, decode2.py (key application and word rescoring)

solution.what: Found nos. 41-42 already deciphered by Lasry (HistoCrypt 2023); established that no. 43 is a different numeric code, not a crib.
Checked Lasry's key against a hand copy of his Figure 8: 234 of 237 pairs fit.
Transcribed nos. 41-42 from the images independently.
Decoded nos. 41-42 with the published key; agrees with Lasry, small corrections added.
Transcribed no. 43 glossed groups with their interlinear readings (about 3,300 pairs) and the 264-group unglossed opening.
Rebuilt the no. 43 key from glosses and layout: interleaved alphabets, syllable blocks of five, underline reverses, nulls 99-250.
Read the unglossed 12-line opening: 220 groups by gloss majority, 24 by structure or nulls, 20 by context.
Scan of ff. 119-120 glosses confirmed 279 de, 364 la, 354 ne; none contradicted.

outcome.method_basis: Nos. 41-42 were read with Lasry's published key and reading (HistoCrypt 2023), in hand before the attempt; the no. 43 code was rebuilt from the contemporary interlinear decipherment on its own leaves and used to read its unglossed 12-line opening.
outcome.notes: Nos. 41-42 re-read from Lasry's key; no. 43 opening is new. 17 of the 20 context-fixed syllable values remain unconfirmed. Attack corrected 22 Sept 2026 from 'known plaintext': first deciphered by Lasry (2023), whose key and reading were in hand; re-deciphered from a fresh transcription (NOTES.md).
